title: Can I make a web game using AI?
author: No-Relief810
selftext: I have zero gaming experience but I am a good web developer in golang and python, i want not just using AI to create game but also using AI to driven it, like NPC conversation , open word etc.

comments.author: Fanof07
comments.body: If you’re curious about making AI driven web games, you might want to check out [onetap.build](https://onetap.build)￼. It lets you turn text prompts into playable worlds with NPC interactions, so you can prototype or experiment with AI-powered gameplay without needing a full game engine. Not a full dev solution for large games, but great for quick, creative projects

comments.author: Slackluster
comments.body:
Yes, I have extensive game dev experience but have been experimenting with fully ai driven coding just to see what is possible and have been very impressed with the results.

LittleJS is an open source game engine that I released about 4 years ago for JS and HTML games. It does not use AI, but I found AI to be very good at using it because of it's size and simplicity. It's possible to create small games directly inside apps like ChatGPT but I recommend a better dev environment like VsCode with Copilot or Codex. You will need to paste errors from the console back to the AI on occasion but it can usually fix with a bit of prompting.

Check out this GitHub repo that shows off what I've made so far. These games were all made without me writing any code! It also includes instructions for AI and templates for the AI to use. You can just fork this repo and start making games with it...

[https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI)

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
What do you mean labeling something AI?

The difference is that would be starting from scratch. This repo contains AI instructions and templates so the AI can work faster and produce better results. I have iterated on many games that are in the repo with the goal of improving the AI instructions and templates.

I mostly use Copilot with Claude Opus 4.6 for working with this repo but I'm interested to hear about other tools people are using like Codex or Cursor.

comments.author: TheKaleKing
comments.body:
Absolutely. I've been using Phaser JS to write a mobile game which is actually a web app wrapped in Capacitor.

I use typescript because I feel like the code is a bit easier to understand but you can absolutely do it. I'd suggest making a solid plan for EVERYTHING unless it's something really small where AI can nail it in one shot. If you're implementing a new system/feature, then creating a plan then having AI execute it 1 step at a time and testing in between has worked wonders for me.

Here's the little project I'm working on. You can tell I love planes: [https://flight747.vercel.app/](https://flight747.vercel.app/)

Have fun with it!

replies.author: TheKaleKing
replies.body:
Haha I don't have clear explanations also it's a bit all over the place right now but basically you can safely run into the planes, they give you XP it's the birds that are little bastards and that we gotta avoid.

Appreciate the feedback! Another thing I wanted to mention is that usually I develop games with unity because I'm most familiar with it but for this project I was curious to see if it would be better with typescript since whenever I work with React apps seems like AI is super sharp and sometimes in Unity it's a little bit lacking.

It's been really impressive, and working really well so far. Go for it! I also saw someone on this sub post a claim that he did a game that he posted in 24 hours which was really nice, and he said it was without an engine like Phaser. He said that AI works best even sometimes without an engine.

I still haven't tested this though, and it could be true but I'm still not sure if the post was 100% legit so take that with a grain of salt but still something that I'm looking foward to test!

comments.author: Cauliflower-Full
comments.body:
Yes, but don’t expect AI to build a full open-world game for you. It works best when you break things into small systems and guide it.  
Core game first → AI features after.
